column4: Visit note | 2025-08-27 10:30 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Arifa Kabir, 43, female. Mrs. Kabir returns for review, stating she has noticed brittle nails, breathlessness on the stairs, and looking pale. She is an accountant and reports these issues started after a stomach illness during a stay in Old Dhaka. She has Essential hypertension. She takes her medicines regularly and reports no bleeding or chest pain. On examination: haemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, BP 142/96 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 47 kg. Conjunctivae are pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-08-27 10:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Rupa Miah, 21, female. Ms. Miah comes for a follow-up visit regarding acne, extra hair on the face, and weight gain. She works as a lawyer and noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Wari. She has no other significant comorbidities. On examination: BMI 27.5, BP 135/74 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 79 kg. Mild facial hirsutism is noted. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-08-27 03:30 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Dalia Hossain, 44, female. Mrs. Hossain presents for her first visit complaining of swelling around the ankle, a twisted ankle, and pain when walking. She is an architect and this injury was twisted during a football match in Savar. She has no chronic comorbidities. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 118/71 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 46 kg. Lateral ankle tenderness and mild swelling are present with stable ligaments. Assessment: Ankle sprain. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use rest, ice, compression, and elevation for 48 hours, and use a crepe bandage. Follow-up in 1 week.
